whoAmI.title: Who am I?
paragraphs: **Data scientist with almost 2 years of experience** in commercial analytics and CRM at **RCM Electrical Cables**. I replaced scattered, outdated Excel spreadsheets, used to calculate KPIs and track the company's metrics, with a **single source of data** fed by a **daily, auditable pipeline**. I developed **3 dashboards** for the executive team: a company-wide overview, sales rep performance and a dedicated customer view. I also developed a **monthly revenue forecast with Prophet** (MAPE, mean absolute percentage error, of **~9%**, up to three months ahead) and a **FastAPI service** that integrates this data into the systems used by the commercial and finance teams. I hold a **bachelor's degree in Physics from UFPR**, with **[international research in computational neuroscience](https://www.budzinskilab.ca)** at the University of Lethbridge (Canada).

During my undergraduate studies, I took part in a project **fine-tuning Cellpose-SAM** to identify and measure neurons in histology, in collaboration with the Pharmacology department, and I am **first author of the resulting paper**. With just **31 annotated images**, AP@50 (average precision at a minimum 50% overlap), the main segmentation metric, rose **from 0.129 to 0.747**, an increase of **nearly 6×**. For neuron counting, the F1-score reached **0.85**. Segmentation went from **~15 minutes to under 10 seconds per image**, with quantified error on the morphometric measurements. The work was presented at the **International Headache Congress (IHC) 2025** and is **under review at Neuroinformatics**.

While still an undergraduate, I was a special student in the graduate course on **Deep Learning**, took subjects such as **Algorithms and Data Structures I** and **Statistics**, and served as project manager at the junior enterprise [Mathmorphosis](https://www.instagram.com/mathmorphosis/), where I **led the team at [UFPR's 1st Data Hackathon](https://ufpr.br/eventos/hackathon-ia/)**, where we took **Top 3**.

contact.title: Contact
contact.text: I'm especially interested in **interdisciplinary problems**, whether they span different departments of a company or pharmacology, neuroscience and physics. :)

items.title: Commercial Analytics Platform — RCM Electrical Cables
items.description: **Replaced scattered spreadsheets** whose indicators disagreed across reports and **made it possible to adopt a source of truth and reference** for the executive board and the commercial teams. I interviewed two departments to turn the business pain into **9 objectives**, and **scoped out 3 unfeasible ones with documented justification before the first line of code**. I built it end to end, on my own: a **daily, auditable pipeline** over two PostgreSQL databases, **LRFM** segmentation, cross-selling, **revenue forecasting with Prophet** and LLM-based sentiment classification. A **statistical detector for out-of-policy discounts** **turned an executive hunch into quantified, auditable evidence**. I cut the pipeline's memory use by **80%**, eliminating failures on 8 GB machines.

items.title: Analytics REST API — RCM Electrical Cables
items.description: **Unlocked the analytics layer**: the analyses were trapped inside Streamlit and no other company system could consume them. In **2 weeks** I built an API in a modular architecture organised by business domain, with **203 endpoints**, a single response contract, Pydantic v2 validation and centralised error handling. I wrote a **coupling smoke test covering 704 calls in ~55s**, which **found 2 real bugs** in the analytics layer, both fixed. **The business logic was left untouched**, and everything was documented with Swagger.

items.title: Institutional Evaluation Platform — UFPR's 1st Data Hackathon
items.description: **Top 3 among more than 10 teams**, and the solution was **considered for future use on the university's platforms**. I **led a team of 3** and, **in 5 days**, we built a visualisation platform over real UFPR institutional evaluation data, with a sentiment index and opinion-balance charts that made legible responses that used to sit in Excel spreadsheets hidden on the university's websites.

items.title: Fine-tuning Cellpose-SAM for Neuron Segmentation
items.description: **An analysis that took ~15 minutes per image now takes under 10 seconds**, enabling large-scale studies of the mechanism behind chronic headache. I adapted a foundation model (Cellpose-SAM) to detect and measure neurons in histology: with **just 31 annotated images**, I raised AP@50 **from 0.129 to 0.747 (nearly 6×)**, with an **F1 of 0.849** and Recall of 0.881 — meaning it finds the vast majority of neurons with few false detections and outlines each precisely enough to measure area and diameter, **with the error of each measurement quantified**. **First author of the paper, under peer review at Neuroinformatics**, with results presented at the **International Headache Congress (IHC) 2025**.

items.title: Theoretical extension to stochastic regimes in complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs)
items.description: Ongoing research supervised by **[Prof. Roberto Budzinski](https://www.ulethbridge.ca/unews/article/university-lethbridge-neuroscientist-receives-canada-research-chair)** in the Department of Neuroscience at the University of Lethbridge.

items.title: This portfolio — context engineering applied to a site
items.description: I built **this site by directing a coding agent through specification**, not ad-hoc prompts. I wrote **9 context documents** (~1,000 lines) defining layout, palette, buttons, background and translation, with a clear rule for which one wins when two specs contradict each other. The agent only executed after reading the context and presenting a plan. Every time it had to **depart from a spec, the reason was logged** in `DECISIONS.md`.
